newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm despite regional weakness.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm despite regional weakness.

text.p: Singapore shares were modestly firmer in active trade on Thursday with interest in second board issues and some blue chips lending support, dealers said.
The Singapore index managed small gains in late afternoon despite sharp falls in the Nikkei and bearish regional bourses.
Electronic stocks continued to draw interest from strong projections for the sector, while sporadic demand was also seen for banks and technology companies, the dealers said.
Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials index closed 10.47 points higher at 2,253.73 on a robust turnaround of 212 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 200 to 179.
The SES Finance Index rose 1.73 points to 516.67, almost matching Wednesday's gains of 1.93 points.
Upbeat prospects for the economy boosted accumulation of bank stocks, which eased in the late afternoon on profit taking.
Top gainers for banks included DBD Foreign shares, up Singapore $0.30 to $19.70, and OCBC Foreign up $0.20 at $18.40.
The biggest loser was Creative Technology, which continued to pare recent gains, falling $0.90 to $14.90.
Second board SM Summit Holdings retained its most active position on a volume of 15.3 million units, up $0.03 to $0.635.
